_meta.note: Merchant-curated pairings. THE single source for what goes with what. Seeded into `product_bundles` by ProductBundleSeeder; read directly by backend/api.js in the static build.
_meta.why: A storefront with no order history has no co-purchase data, and calling a guess 'frequently bought together' is a claim about other customers that has not happened. These are pairings the merchant stands behind, labelled as such. BundleService prefers real co-purchase counts the moment enough orders exist, and only then does the wording change to 'frequently bought together'.
_meta.rule: Every bundle states WHY its members belong together, in `reason`, in words a customer would recognise. If a reason cannot be written, the bundle is not real and should not ship.

bundles.title: The iftar table
bundles.reason: Dates to break the fast, honey for the drink that follows, pistachios for the plate that sits between them. The three things that end up on the same table every evening of Ramadan.

bundles.title: Both dates, side by side
bundles.reason: Ajwa is dense and barely sweet; Sukkari is soft and honeyed. Most households end up keeping both, because they are not eaten for the same reason.

bundles.title: The biryani corner
bundles.reason: Saffron bloomed in warm milk and ghee to fry the onions in — the two things a pot of biryani cannot fake with anything else.

bundles.title: Fill the nut jar
bundles.reason: Cashews to cook with, pistachios to snack on, figs for the sweet end of the same bowl. Buying the three together is how most kitchens stay stocked.

bundles.title: A gift that needs no wrapping
bundles.reason: The saffron arrives boxed and the mix arrives sealed in glass. Together they cover the two people you never know what to buy for.

bundles.title: The morning spoon
bundles.reason: Black seed oil is sharp enough that most people take it stirred into honey rather than neat. Sidr is thick enough to carry it.

bundles.title: Dress it and finish it
bundles.reason: Cold-pressed olive oil and dried oregano are the two things a salad, a flatbread and a plate of pasta all want, and neither survives being cooked hard.

bundles.title: Buffalo and cow, both jars
bundles.reason: Buffalo ghee sets harder and browns later, so it goes in the pan; hand-churned cow ghee has the aroma, so it goes on the roti. Cooks who keep one usually end up keeping both.

bundles.title: The cold-pressed pair
bundles.reason: Sesame for everyday heat, olive for everything served cold. Between them they cover a week of cooking without a refined oil in the house.
